shortDescription: Manages external LTM monitors on a BIG-IP

options.name: arguments
options.description: Specifies any command-line arguments the script requires.

options.name: external_program
options.description: Specifies the name of the file for the monitor to use. In order to reference a file, you must first import it using options on the B(System > File Management > External Monitor Program File List > Import) screen. The BIG-IP system automatically places the file in the proper location on the file system.

options.name: interval
options.description: The interval specifying how frequently the monitor instance of this template will run. If this parameter is not provided when creating a new monitor, the default value will be 5. This value B(must) be less than the C(timeout) value.

options.name: ip
options.description: IP address part of the IP/port definition. If this parameter is not provided when creating a new monitor, the default value will be '*'.

options.name: name
options.description: Specifies the name of the monitor.

options.name: parent
options.description: The parent template of this monitor template. Once this value has been set, it cannot be changed. By default, this value is the C(external) parent on the C(Common) partition.

options.name: partition
options.description: Device partition to manage resources on.

options.name: port
options.description: Port address part of the IP/port definition. If this parameter is not provided when creating a new monitor, then the default value will be '*'. If specifying an IP address, you must use a value between 1 and 65535.

options.name: provider
options.description: A dict object containing connection details.

options.name: state
options.description: When C(present), ensures the monitor exists. When C(absent), ensures the monitor is removed.

options.name: timeout
options.description: The number of seconds in which the node or service must respond to the monitor request. If the target responds within the set time period, it is considered up. If the target does not respond within the set time period, it is considered down. You can change this to any number, however, it should be 3 times the interval number of seconds plus 1 second. If this parameter is not provided when creating a new monitor, the default value will be C(16).

options.name: variables
options.description: Specifies any variables the script requires. Note that double quotes in values will be suppressed.
